```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Krause_2026_warfarin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Krause_2026_warfarin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-026-10053-8>

Krause and Celliere (2026) is a tutorial on deriving pediatric doses from an
adult population PK model by steady-state exposure matching. The worked example
is an adult two-compartment warfarin model, fitted in Monolix to the single-dose
O'Reilly warfarin dataset, with body weight on every clearance and volume
through allometric exponents fixed to 0.75 and 1. That model is packaged here.
The paper then uses it to find, for each body weight from 10 to 75 kg, the
once-daily dose whose steady-state Cmax, Ctrough or AUC matches a 75 kg adult
taking 10 mg once daily, and to turn those optimum doses into a dosing table
under three strategies (best fit, conservative, progressive). This article
repeats that whole workflow with the packaged model.

The authors deposited their Monolix project, data and R/Simulx scripts, and
the outputs those scripts produced, as Supplementary Material 2. Those outputs
give exact reference values, and the checks below compare against them.

# Population

Thirty-two adults aged 21 to 63 years received a single oral warfarin loading
dose of 1.5 mg/kg (60 to 153 mg). Plasma concentrations were measured at 1, 2,
3, 6, 9 and 12 h after the dose in 14 subjects and at 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and
120 h in all subjects, 247 concentrations in total. The article prints no
demographics table; from the deposited dataset, body weight ranged from 40 to
102 kg (median 71.65 kg), median age was 27.5 years, and 5 of the 32 subjects
(15.6%) were female.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
readModelDb("Krause_2026_warfarin")()$population
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value is the full-precision estimate in the deposited
`populationParameters.txt` of the Monolix run
`Warfarin-TwoCompLinPKAllomScalingBW`, the run named as the model in the
deposited `101-Setup.R`. Table 2 of the article prints the same estimates
rounded.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `ltlag` | log(0.7352) h | Table 2 tlag 0.74 h |
| `lka` | log(0.9591) 1/h | Table 2 ka 0.96 1/h |
| `lcl` | log(0.1393) L/h | Table 2 CL 0.14 L/h |
| `lvc` | log(6.567) L | Table 2 Vc 6.57 L |
| `lq` | log(3.839) L/h | Table 2 Q 3.84 L/h |
| `lvp` | log(2.123) L | Table 2 Vp 2.12 L |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_q` | 0.75, held constant | Table 2 beta CL / beta Q, body weight 0.75 |
| `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_vp` | 1, held constant | Table 2 beta Vc / beta Vp, body weight 1.00 |
| `etaltlag` | 0.3108 (omega 0.557) | Table 2 tlag random-effect SD 0.56, 60.4 %CV |
| `etalka` | 0.5458 (omega 0.739) | Table 2 ka random-effect SD 0.74, 85.2 %CV |
| `etalcl` | 0.06821 (omega 0.261) | Table 2 CL random-effect SD 0.26, 26.6 %CV |
| `etalvc` | 0.004829 (omega 0.0695) | Table 2 Vc random-effect SD 0.07, 7.00 %CV |
| `etalq` | 6.210 (omega 2.49) | Table 2 Q random-effect SD 2.49, 2228.9 %CV |
| `etalvp` | 0.2026 (omega 0.450) | Table 2 Vp random-effect SD 0.45, 47.4 %CV |
| `addSd` | 0.2073 mg/L | Table 2 error parameter a 0.21 |
| `propSd` | 0.04852 | Table 2 error parameter b 0.05 |
| `(WT / 75)^e` on CL, Q, Vc, Vp | n/a | Supplementary Material 1, covariate equations; mlxtran `logtWt = log(wt/75)` |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)`, `alag(depot)` | n/a | Supplementary Material 1, Monolix `pkmodel(Tlag, ka, V, Cl, k12, k21)` with `k12 = Q/V1`, `k21 = Q/V2` |
| `Cc ~ add(addSd) + prop(propSd) + combined1()` | n/a | mlxtran `errorModel = combined1(a1, b1)` |

# Steady-state exposure of the typical subject

The paper defines steady state as the 30th once-daily dose: exposure is taken
over 696 to 720 h, with concentrations output every 0.2 h (deposited
`101-Setup.R`). Cmax is the largest concentration in that window, Ctrough the
last one (at 720 h, 24 h after the 30th dose) and AUC the integral over the
window. Because the model is linear, exposure is proportional to dose, so one
typical subject per weight on 1 mg once daily is enough; every other dose is a
multiple of it.

```{r typical-sim}
mod <- readModelDb("Krause_2026_warfarin")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ss_window <- c(696, 720)
dose_times <- seq(0, 696, by = 24)
obs_times <- round(seq(ss_window[1], ss_window[2], by = 0.2), 1)

make_ss_events <- function(wt, dose, id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_along(wt)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    data.frame(id = ids, WT = wt, dose = dose),
    time = dose_times
  ) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    data.frame(id = ids, WT = wt, dose = dose),
    time = obs_times
  ) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

weights_fine <- seq(10, 75, by = 2.5)
ev_typ <- make_ss_events(weights_fine, dose = 1)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  events = ev_typ,
  keep = c("WT", "dose"),
  rtol = 1e-10,
  atol = 1e-12,
  maxsteps = 1e6,
  omega = NA,
  sigma = NA
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

The steady-state exposures are computed with PKNCA, one interval per typical
subject (`cmax`, `clast.obs` -- the last concentration of the window, which is the
paper's Ctrough -- and a linear-trapezoid `auclast` over 696-720 h).

```{r typical-pknca}
conc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, WT)
dose_typ <- ev_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, WT)

nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_typ, Cc ~ time | WT + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_typ, amt ~ time | WT + id),
    intervals = data.frame(
      start = ss_window[1],
      end = ss_window[2],
      cmax = TRUE,
      clast.obs = TRUE,
      auclast = TRUE
    ),
    options = list(auc.method = "linear")
  )
)

per_mg <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  select(WT, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  mutate(
    metric = c(cmax = "Cmax", clast.obs = "Ctrough", auclast = "AUC")[PPTESTCD]
  ) |>
  select(WT, metric, per_mg = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(per_mg) == 3 * length(weights_fine), !anyNA(per_mg$per_mg))
```

The deposited file `R/output.data/data-exposures.txt` lists the typical-subject
exposures the authors' Simulx run produced for every weight and dose of the
grid. The rows below are its 10 mg values at four weights.

```{r typical-compare}
deposited_10mg <- tibble::tribble(
  ~WT, ~cmax,   ~clast.obs, ~auclast,
  10,  16.9102, 10.1502,  325.264,
  30,  7.05289, 4.78473,  142.703,
  50,  4.71599, 3.35043,  97.2921,
  75,  3.43193, 2.51878,  71.7854
) |>
  mutate(WT = as.character(WT))

sim_10mg <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  filter(WT %in% c(10, 30, 50, 75)) |>
  mutate(WT = as.character(WT), PPORRES = 10 * PPORRES) |>
  select(WT, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

cmp_typ <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_10mg,
  reference = deposited_10mg,
  by = "WT",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", clast.obs = "mg/L", auclast = "h*mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 1
)
cmp_typ |>
  dplyr::rename("Body weight (kg)" = WT) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "Typical-subject steady-state exposure on 10 mg once daily: packaged",
      "model (Simulated) against the authors' deposited Simulx output",
      "(Reference)."
    )
  )

pct_diff <- with(
  inner_join(
    sim_10mg,
    pivot_longer(deposited_10mg, -WT, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("WT", "PPTESTCD")
  ),
  100 * (PPORRES / ref - 1)
)
# Deterministic comparison (typical subject, same output grid); the measured
# agreement is better than 0.05 %. A transcription error in any parameter or
# in the 75 kg reference weight moves these by whole percent.
stopifnot(length(pct_diff) == 12L, max(abs(pct_diff)) < 0.5)

# At steady state the AUC over one dosing interval equals dose / CL.
cl_75 <- exp(rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta[["lcl"]])
auc_ref <- per_mg$per_mg[per_mg$WT == 75 & per_mg$metric == "AUC"] * 10
stopifnot(abs(auc_ref / (10 / cl_75) - 1) < 1e-3)
```

The packaged model reproduces the authors' typical-subject exposures to within
0.05% at every weight and metric, and the 75 kg reference AUC equals
10 mg / CL = `r signif(10 / cl_75, 4)` h*mg/L.

# Optimum doses on the fine grid (Figure 3)

The fine grid uses doses from 0 to 10 mg in 0.2 mg steps. For each weight and
metric the optimum dose is the one whose exposure lies closest to the reference
exposure of a 75 kg adult on 10 mg (the best-fit rule of Table 1). The
conservative and progressive rules of Table 1 are written out alongside it;
when two doses tie, the lower dose is taken, as in the authors' code.

```{r fine-grid}
ref_exposure <- per_mg |>
  filter(WT == 75) |>
  transmute(metric, ref = 10 * per_mg)

exposure_grid <- function(doses, weights) {
  per_mg |>
    filter(WT %in% weights) |>
    tidyr::crossing(dose = doses) |>
    mutate(value = per_mg * dose) |>
    left_join(ref_exposure, by = "metric") |>
    mutate(delta = value - ref)
}

optimum_dose <- function(dose, delta, strategy) {
  o <- order(dose)
  dose <- dose[o]
  delta <- delta[o]
  switch(
    strategy,
    "Best fit" = dose[which.min(abs(delta))],
    "Conservative" = if (any(delta <= 0)) max(dose[delta <= 0]) else 0,
    "Progressive" = if (any(delta >= 0)) min(dose[delta >= 0]) else 0
  )
}

fine_doses <- round(seq(0, 10, by = 0.2), 1)
grid_fine <- exposure_grid(fine_doses, weights_fine)
opt_fine <- grid_fine |>
  group_by(metric, WT) |>
  summarise(
    dose = optimum_dose(dose, delta, "Best fit"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(opt_fine, aes(WT, dose, colour = metric)) +
  geom_step(direction = "mid") +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)",
    y = "Optimum dose (mg)",
    colour = "Exposure metric",
    title = "Optimum dose by body weight (best fit, fine grid)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Krause 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The Results section reports the optimum doses at 10, 30 and 50 kg; the packaged
model returns them exactly. The deposited `Table-Dosing-Recommendation-Fine.txt`
holds all 81 best-fit optimum doses (27 weights by 3 metrics), and the packaged
model reproduces every one of them as well (checked while preparing this
article; the file is not shipped with the package).

```{r figure-3-check}
published_opt <- tibble::tribble(
  ~WT, ~metric,   ~published,
  10,  "Cmax",    2.0,
  10,  "AUC",     2.2,
  10,  "Ctrough", 2.4,
  30,  "Cmax",    4.8,
  30,  "AUC",     5.0,
  30,  "Ctrough", 5.2,
  50,  "Cmax",    7.2,
  50,  "AUC",     7.4,
  50,  "Ctrough", 7.6
)
chk_opt <- inner_join(published_opt, opt_fine, by = c("WT", "metric"))
chk_opt |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Body weight (kg)" = WT,
    "Exposure metric" = metric,
    "Published optimum (mg)" = published,
    "Packaged model (mg)" = dose
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Optimum doses quoted in the Results section.")
stopifnot(nrow(chk_opt) == 9L, all(abs(chk_opt$dose - chk_opt$published) < 1e-8))
```

# Dosing table from the available doses (Table 3, Figure 4)

The available doses are 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 mg and the body weight category
limits are 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 and 75 kg. Applying each Table 1 rule at
each category limit gives the optimum available dose there.

```{r available}
weights_steps <- c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 75)
grid_avail <- exposure_grid(seq(0, 10, by = 2), weights_steps)
strategies <- c("Best fit", "Conservative", "Progressive")

opt_avail <- tidyr::crossing(
  strategy = strategies,
  grid_avail |> distinct(metric, WT)
)
opt_avail$dose <- mapply(
  function(s, m, w) {
    g <- grid_avail[grid_avail$metric == m & grid_avail$WT == w, ]
    optimum_dose(g$dose, g$delta, s)
  },
  opt_avail$strategy,
  opt_avail$metric,
  opt_avail$WT
)
```

Table 3 of the paper turns these into weight bands. Read at the category
limits, its bands give the doses below; the packaged model reproduces every
cell.

```{r table-3}
# Dose at each category limit (10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 75 kg) read from the
# Table 3 weight bands. Progressive Ctrough uses the deposited
# Table-Dosing-Recommendation-Available.txt band 50.01-75 kg for 10 mg; Table 3
# prints that band as '>40 - 75', which overlaps the 8 mg band above it.
table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~strategy,      ~metric,   ~doses,
  "Best fit",     "AUC",     c(2, 4, 6, 6, 8, 8, 10),
  "Best fit",     "Cmax",    c(2, 4, 4, 6, 8, 8, 10),
  "Best fit",     "Ctrough", c(2, 4, 6, 6, 8, 8, 10),
  "Conservative", "AUC",     c(2, 2, 4, 6, 6, 8, 10),
  "Conservative", "Cmax",    c(2, 2, 4, 6, 6, 8, 10),
  "Conservative", "Ctrough", c(2, 2, 4, 6, 6, 8, 10),
  "Progressive",  "AUC",     c(4, 4, 6, 8, 8, 10, 10),
  "Progressive",  "Cmax",    c(4, 4, 6, 8, 8, 10, 10),
  "Progressive",  "Ctrough", c(4, 4, 6, 8, 8, 10, 10)
) |>
  tidyr::unnest(doses) |>
  group_by(strategy, metric) |>
  mutate(WT = weights_steps) |>
  ungroup() |>
  rename(published = doses)

chk_avail <- inner_join(table3, opt_avail, by = c("strategy", "metric", "WT"))
stopifnot(nrow(chk_avail) == 63L, all(chk_avail$dose == chk_avail$published))

opt_avail |>
  mutate(WT = paste(WT, "kg")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = WT, values_from = dose) |>
  dplyr::rename("Strategy" = strategy, "Exposure metric" = metric) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "Optimum available dose (mg) at each category limit; identical to",
      "Table 3 of Krause 2026 in all 63 cells."
    )
  )
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = opt_fine,
    aes(WT, dose),
    colour = "grey50",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_step(
    data = opt_avail,
    aes(WT, dose, colour = strategy),
    direction = "mid"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = opt_avail, aes(WT, dose, colour = strategy)) +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)",
    y = "Dose (mg)",
    colour = "Strategy",
    title = "Dosing schemes by strategy",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Krause 2026. Dashed: fine-grid optimum dose;",
      "points: optimum available dose at the category limits."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Deviation from the reference exposure (Figure 5)

Between the category limits the dosing table assigns one of the neighbouring
available doses, so exposure departs most from the reference at the limits
where the dose changes. Figure 5 plots the percentage deviation of the exposure
reached with the optimum available dose at each fine-grid weight.

```{r figure-5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
deviation <- tidyr::crossing(
  strategy = strategies,
  grid_avail |> distinct(metric),
  WT = weights_fine
)
grid_avail_fine <- exposure_grid(seq(0, 10, by = 2), weights_fine)
deviation$dose <- mapply(
  function(s, m, w) {
    g <- grid_avail_fine[grid_avail_fine$metric == m & grid_avail_fine$WT == w, ]
    optimum_dose(g$dose, g$delta, s)
  },
  deviation$strategy,
  deviation$metric,
  deviation$WT
)
deviation <- deviation |>
  left_join(per_mg, by = c("metric", "WT")) |>
  left_join(ref_exposure, by = "metric") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (per_mg * dose / ref - 1))

ggplot(deviation, aes(WT, pct, colour = strategy)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)",
    y = "Exposure deviation from reference (%)",
    colour = "Strategy",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Krause 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

dev_prog_cmax_10 <- deviation$pct[
  deviation$strategy == "Progressive" &
    deviation$metric == "Cmax" &
    deviation$WT == 10
]
dev_cons_20 <- deviation |>
  filter(strategy == "Conservative", WT == 20) |>
  select(metric, pct)
# Typical-subject (deterministic) values. The paper quotes them in round
# words ('nearly twice', '40% less'); the bounds test that reading.
stopifnot(
  dev_prog_cmax_10 > 80,
  dev_prog_cmax_10 < 110,
  all(dev_cons_20$pct < -35),
  all(dev_cons_20$pct > -55)
)
```

The paper notes that with the progressive strategy and the Cmax metric a 10 kg
child would reach nearly twice the intended exposure; the packaged model gives
`r sprintf("%+.0f%%", dev_prog_cmax_10)`. It also notes that with the
conservative strategy a 20 kg child would reach about 40% less exposure than
targeted for every metric; the packaged model gives
`r paste(sprintf("%s %+.0f%%", dev_cons_20$metric, dev_cons_20$pct), collapse = ", ")`.

# Exposure with inter-individual variability (Figure 6)

To place the dosing table in the context of PK variability, the paper simulates
100 subjects per body weight on the dose assigned to that weight and compares
the 90% prediction interval of each exposure metric with that of the reference
adult (75 kg, 10 mg once daily). The cohort below does the same for the
best-fit, AUC-based dose at each category limit, with 100 subjects per weight.

```{r iiv-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_per_weight <- 100L
bf_auc <- opt_avail |>
  filter(strategy == "Best fit", metric == "AUC")
ev_iiv <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(bf_auc)), function(i) {
  make_ss_events(
    wt = rep(bf_auc$WT[i], n_per_weight),
    dose = bf_auc$dose[i],
    id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_weight
  )
}))
stopifnot(length(unique(ev_iiv$id)) == n_per_weight * nrow(bf_auc))

sim_iiv <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_iiv,
  keep = c("WT", "dose"),
  maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Same definitions as the authors' Simulx outcomes: maximum and last
# concentration in the window, and the trapezoidal integral of Cc over it.
exp_iiv <- sim_iiv |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  group_by(id, WT, dose) |>
  summarise(
    Cmax = max(Cc),
    Ctrough = Cc[time == ss_window[2]],
    AUC = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cmax, Ctrough, AUC), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")
stopifnot(nrow(exp_iiv) == 3L * n_per_weight * nrow(bf_auc), !anyNA(exp_iiv$value))
```

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
pi_iiv <- exp_iiv |>
  group_by(metric, WT, dose) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(value, 0.05),
    q50 = median(value),
    q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pi_ref <- pi_iiv |>
  filter(WT == 75) |>
  select(metric, q05, q50, q95) |>
  pivot_longer(-metric, names_to = "quantile", values_to = "value")

ggplot(pi_iiv, aes(WT)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q50), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(
    data = pi_ref,
    aes(yintercept = value, linetype = quantile == "q50"),
    colour = "grey30",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)",
    y = "Steady-state exposure (mg/L; h*mg/L for AUC)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the best-fit AUC panel of Figure 6 of Krause 2026.",
      "Band: 90% prediction interval at the dose assigned to each weight;",
      "lines: median and 90% interval of the 75 kg, 10 mg reference."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The deposited `data-exposures-iiv.txt` holds the authors' 100 simulated
reference subjects (75 kg, 10 mg once daily). The comparison below uses its
5th, 50th and 95th percentiles. Both sides are random samples of 100 subjects,
so the check is on the centre and on generous bounds for the tails.

```{r figure-6-check}
deposited_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~metric,   ~q05,  ~q50, ~q95,
  "AUC",     47.4,  71.2, 110,
  "Cmax",    2.53,  3.39, 5.09,
  "Ctrough", 1.58,  2.49, 3.97
)
chk_ref <- pi_iiv |>
  filter(WT == 75) |>
  select(metric, q05, q50, q95) |>
  inner_join(deposited_ref, by = "metric", suffix = c("_sim", "_dep"))

chk_ref |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Exposure metric" = metric,
    "5th pct, simulated" = q05_sim,
    "5th pct, deposited" = q05_dep,
    "Median, simulated" = q50_sim,
    "Median, deposited" = q50_dep,
    "95th pct, simulated" = q95_sim,
    "95th pct, deposited" = q95_dep
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = paste(
      "Reference adult (75 kg, 10 mg once daily): steady-state exposure",
      "quantiles from 100 simulated subjects, packaged model against the",
      "authors' deposited simulation (mg/L; h*mg/L for AUC)."
    )
  )

# With omega(CL) = 0.26, the median of 100 subjects has a standard error of
# about 3 % and the 5th / 95th percentiles about 5-6 %, on each side. A
# wrong omega (variance read as SD) or a wrong reference weight moves the
# median or the tail by well over these bounds. Realised worst cases over
# five cohorts (2 and 16 solver threads): median 4.4 %, 5th percentile 10 %,
# 95th percentile 18 %.
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk_ref) == 3L,
  all(abs(chk_ref$q50_sim / chk_ref$q50_dep - 1) < 0.12),
  all(abs(chk_ref$q05_sim / chk_ref$q05_dep - 1) < 0.25),
  all(abs(chk_ref$q95_sim / chk_ref$q95_dep - 1) < 0.25)
)
```

# Single-dose profiles (Figure S1)

Figure S1 shows typical concentration-time profiles after a single 1.5 mg/kg
dose for 50 kg and 75 kg subjects.

```{r figure-s1, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ev_sd <- bind_rows(lapply(c(50, 75), function(w) {
  id <- match(w, c(50, 75))
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, WT = w, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 1.5 * w, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(
      id = id,
      WT = w,
      time = seq(0, 144, by = 0.5),
      evid = 0L,
      amt = 0,
      cmt = "central"
    )
  )
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  events = ev_sd,
  keep = "WT",
  omega = NA,
  sigma = NA
) |>
  as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_sd, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(WT))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Warfarin concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = "Body weight (kg)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the allometric-model curves of Figure S1 of Krause 2026",
      "(typical subjects, single 1.5 mg/kg dose)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Final model only.** Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 report two alternative
  fits (all four weight exponents estimated; the exponent on Q removed). The
  authors selected the fixed-allometry model of Table 2 on BICc and used it for
  every dose derivation, so only that model is packaged.
- **Full-precision estimates.** Table 2 rounds the estimates to two significant
  figures (CL 0.14 L/h). The packaged values are the full-precision estimates
  of the deposited Monolix run, which agree with Table 2 to its printed
  precision and reproduce the authors' exposures to better than 0.05%; the
  rounded values would shift the reference exposure by about 0.5%.
- **Residual error form.** Monolix `combined1` is `y = Cc + (a + b * Cc) * e`,
  which is `combined1()` in nlmixr2 (the nlmixr2 default, `combined2`, adds
  the two variances instead).
- **Concentration units.** Doses are in mg and volumes in L, so `Cc` is in
  mg/L, the unit of the deposited dataset (for example 9.2 mg/L at 24 h after
  100 mg). The Figure 6 caption gives the units as ng/mL; the exposures in the
  deposited output (reference Cmax 3.43, AUC 71.8 = 10 mg / 0.139 L/h) are in
  mg/L and h*mg/L. The deposited model folder also contains a variant with
  `Cc2 = 1000 * Cc`, but the deposited setup simulates `Cc`.
- **Table 3 typo.** The last band of the progressive / Ctrough row of Table 3
  reads '>40 - 75' kg for 10 mg, overlapping the 8 mg band '>30 - 50' kg. The
  deposited `Table-Dosing-Recommendation-Available.txt` gives 50.01-75 kg, the
  same as for the other two metrics, and the packaged model agrees.
- **Figure S1 caption.** The caption gives the 1.5 mg/kg doses for 50 and 75 kg
  as 75 and 107.5 mg; 1.5 mg/kg at 75 kg is 112.5 mg, which is what is
  simulated here.
- **Covariates not used.** Sex and age are in the deposited dataset and are
  declared in the Monolix project but enter no parameter model; they are
  documented under `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Inter-individual variability on Q.** The random-effect SD on Q is 2.49
  (2229 %CV) and the standard error of Q itself is about 10^5 L/h (Table 2), so
  Q is barely identifiable from these data. The value is packaged as
  estimated. Individual Q values span several orders of magnitude in
  simulation, which mainly affects Cmax; AUC is set by CL.
- **Not a dosing recommendation.** The authors stress that the warfarin
  example illustrates exposure matching only. Warfarin is titrated to INR in
  practice, and the model carries no maturation, so it should not be used
  below about 10 kg (roughly 2 years of age).
- No erratum or correction notice for the article was found as of 2026-11-15.
